verdict: Mosaic swung to a $72M loss as phosphate margins collapsed — it lost money on every tonne of phosphate sold — while its potash mines stayed solidly profitable.

segments.name: Phosphate
segments.note: Phosphate fertilizers made in Florida and Louisiana. Sales held near $1.3B, but the segment lost $194M from operations — production was cut back to match scarce, expensive sulfur supply.

segments.name: Mosaic Fertilizantes
segments.note: The Brazilian fertilizer production and distribution business. Sales here are the remainder after the two segments Mosaic details (its release rounds Fertilizantes sales to $1.3B including items eliminated in consolidation); the segment lost $21M from operations.

segments.name: Potash
segments.note: Potash mined in Saskatchewan and New Mexico — the profit anchor, with $189M of operating earnings and a $97 gross margin per tonne.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling fertilizer worldwide and running the company.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Other operating costs, including items tied to idled or curtailed phosphate capacity.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $60M, partly offset by a $38M foreign-currency transaction gain and $15M of other income.
oneTimers: Phosphate economics were the story: the segment's gross margin was negative $105 per tonne in the quarter (vs +$92 a year ago) as sulfur — a key input Mosaic must buy — stayed scarce and expensive, and Mosaic curtailed production to match. Adjusted EPS of $0.19 excludes notable items including the currency gain.
follow100Note: A loss quarter: Mosaic spent $2.32 more per $100 of sales than it kept — the shortfall was covered by cash on hand. The tax line is a benefit (money back).

takeaways.title: Phosphate lost money per tonne
takeaways.text: Phosphate gross margin swung from +$92 to -$105 per tonne in a year as sulfur costs spiked and prices lagged. The segment lost $194M from operations.

takeaways.title: Potash paid the bills
takeaways.text: Potash earned $189M from operations on $643M of sales — a reminder that Mosaic's two nutrient businesses can move in opposite directions.

takeaways.title: Almost no cushion at the top line
takeaways.text: Consolidated gross margin was just 2.7% (from 16.0%), so ordinary running costs were enough to push the quarter into a loss despite a $38M currency gain and a $38M tax benefit.

footerNote: Figures are rounded to whole $M from the release's one-decimal presentation, with minor rounding absorbed in the small lines. The tax line is a $38M benefit. Net loss attributable to Mosaic was $72M; the consolidated loss was $65M, with $7M of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests.
